title: Anthropic Opens Critical Infrastructure AI Probe to US Government Agencies
summary:
Anthropic has merged Project Glasswing and its Cyber Verification Program into a unified three tier system to provide vetted security professionals with graded access to permissive AI models. Organizations vetted by the US government are permitted to use Claude to probe critical infrastructure, including power grids, interbank networks and flight systems, while penetration testing firms can use the AI to break into client systems for authorized work. Lower access tiers for independent researchers and hospital security teams enable malware analysis and flaw patching but prohibit offensive attacks. The updated program grants access to Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.

The expansion follows data showing that Zhipu AI's open GLM-5.3 model created working exploits in 50 of 410 attempts, nearly matching the 56 produced by Mythos Preview. Anthropic argues that withholding Mythos primarily hinders security defenders because attackers can strip safety refusals from rival models using roughly $4,400 in compute. Previously, partners in the Glasswing program identified at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July, with more than 33,000 of those flaws classified as critical or high severity.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic is opening Claude Mythos 5.1 to vetted cyber defenders through 3 access tiers that absorb Project Glasswing. 

Until now, only Glasswing members got Mythos, while the Cyber Verification Program loosened filters on Opus and Sonnet for vetted security teams. 

Anthropic ran Opus 5.5 through its CyScenarioBench attack scenarios 50 times per tier, and without program access every run stopped at the first prompt. 
anthropic

Claude now gives more hacking help the more Anthropic trusts you and the more dangerous the systems you are allowed to attack.

A hospital security team or a lone researcher gets help analyzing malware and fixing flaws, but Claude won't help them attack anything.

A penetration-testing firm can also have Claude break into client systems it is hired to test, though ransomware stays blocked.

Only organizations vetted with the US government can use Claude to probe power grids, flight systems and interbank networks.

The expansion follows Anthropic's finding that Zhipu AI's freely downloadable GLM-5.3 built working exploits in 50 of 410 attempts, nearly matching Mythos Preview's 56.

Anyone can strip that model's safety refusals, as Anthropic did for about $4,400 of compute, so attackers already have near-Mythos exploit skills and so in many sense withholding Mythos mostly handicaps defenders.
